correctness.rationale: The exact quadratic transformation separates the central scalar recurrence from a stochastic three-kernel product. Its sum-zero trace, determinant and discriminant are factored exactly; only one interior discriminant root exists. Permutation conjugation covers all six calendars. The nonzero antisymmetric entry rules out a diagonalizable repeated eigenvalue, and Cayley-Hamilton gives the exact Jordan powers for every integer iteration. The standalone symbolic checker confirms critical algebra and rational original-system iterates; finite examples are not treated as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Primary paper Jamilov 2022/2023 develops the family for a single fixed permutation and does not present the all-three-transposition seasonal spectrum. The earlier two-season exceptional-point claim is excluded rather than relabeled: the three-factor matrix has a different factored discriminant and reverses the real-to-complex phase direction. Actual published-finding corpus queries and targeted literature searches found no stronger exact all-calendar statement; inaccessible publisher texts and general matrix-product coverage remain explicit risks.

value.rationale: Three distinct pairwise exchanges form the shortest complete schedule on the peripheral triangle, rather than an arbitrary extra season. Simultaneously classifying all six calendar orders gives a unique exact threshold, a reversal of the two-edge spectral phase and a genuine defectiveness criterion with exact polynomial correction to convergence. These facts explain qualitative transient dynamics in the full naturally complete interaction protocol and are not implied by the fixed-permutation equilibrium theorem.
